- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Model overestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true prices show strong upward momentum.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: forecasts too aggressively revert to historical lows, missing sustained upward trends.
- Model lags behind true price movements by 2–5 days, especially in upward trends — forecasts are too early to capture momentum.
- When true prices spike, model forecasts overshoot the peak and then overcorrect, creating a “double dip” pattern.
- Model underestimates volatility in the final 5–7 days, leading to overly conservative forecasts near the end of the horizon.
- Model tends to underestimate the magnitude of price corrections after spikes — fails to recognize the “rebound” phase.
- Model shows persistent bias toward lower values in the first 10 days of the forecast, especially when history shows recent volatility.
